newsitem.title: THAILAND: Degussa unit to open Thai jewellery alloy plant.
newsitem.headline: Degussa unit to open Thai jewellery alloy plant.

text.p: Degussa (Thailand) Ltd, an affiliate of Frankfurt-based Degussa AG, said on Wednesday it would open Thailand's first jewellery alloy plant in Bangkok next month.
The plant worth 56 million baht ($2.15 million) will initially produce 4.0 tonnes of fine gold per year and the company hopes to capture 20 percent of the total Thai market in the future.
Degussa told a news conference the local industry currently consumes about 110 tonnes of 99.99 percent fine gold and 1,000 metric tonnes of 99.9 percent of fine silver annually.
Volker Schmidt, managing director of Degussa (Thailand) Ltd, said the operation would enhance and reinforce Thailand's stance as one of the world's major precious metal centres.
"It also demonstrates our ongoing commitment to Thailand and, in particular, its jewellery sectors. This is the first of a new series of investments by Degussa in Thailand," Schmidt said.
The operation would initially concentrate on precious metal refining. At a later stage, the Degussa plant would produce jewellery alloys.

Schmidt said the Degussa plant would lead to significant savings to the Thai jewellery sector because some of the facilities that the company would offer have not previously been available in Thailand.
Savings will be made in foreign exchange transactions, local production of jewellery alloys, processing times of scrap to fine gold and the elimination of precious metal wastage.
The plant could save Thailand about 1.2 billion baht annually in foreign exchange, he added.
Degussa AG holds 49 percent of its Thai affiliate and Thai investors the remainder.
